contributions.title: create_market accounts a market for total_pool = net_amount but funds each side with the truncated quotient, so up to side_count - 1 lamports in a market belong to no side, and claim_winnings - which divides each bet by the winning sides' stored totals, not by the pool - can be asked to pay lamports

alternatives: Diagnosis, offered as hypothesis rather than observation: under the truncated accounting the winning sides' stored totals sum to less than the pool, so the final winning claim transfers more lamports than the market still attributes and either fails or leaves the market short by the residue.
Alternative A: leave truncation in place and add a sweep or close instruction that moves the residue out of the market to the creator.
Alternative B: make the accounting self-consistent by rounding the pool down - total_pool = amount_per_side * side_count - and refunding the residue to the creator inside create_market.
Alternative C: credit the whole residue to one designated side (index 0) instead of one lamport each to the first `remainder` sides, reducing the branch to a single special case.

Alternative D, the candidate as written: spread one lamport across the first `remainder` sides and mirror market.sides[i].total_amount into the creator's bets, which makes creation-time accounting exact without new instructions.
narrative.integration: Integrate the candidate as the lab's account-reconciling create_market change on the exact SHA b3248454, and change nothing else. Sequence: (a) land it on lab main through the protected workflow so the reviewed, attested object is the same SHA the evidence names; (b) before any behavioural statement is made, add the missing runtime fixture - a local-validator round trip over 2 to 10 sides at 1, 2 and 3 SOL including a residue case, devnet-grade with no mainnet keys and no key material - because the current fixture is build-only and never executes create_market; (c) keep the frontend in step by reading displayed side splits from market.sides[].total_amount rather than recomputing a quotient client-side, since address derivation is unaffected because the seed is unchanged; (d) document the residue rule so integrators know the first `remainder` sides in the supplied order carry one extra lamport. No production deployment, no upstream merge and no acceptance claim are part of this proposal.
limitations: Narrative drafted by the Sol.College CTO agent; authoritative fields (commits, evidence, hashes) are assembled by code.
narrative.problem: create_market accounts a market for total_pool = net_amount but funds each side with the truncated quotient, so up to side_count - 1 lamports in a market belong to no side, and claim_winnings - which divides each bet by the winning sides' stored totals, not by the pool - can be asked to pay lamports the market cannot attribute. Candidate b3248454 computes the residue once with checked_rem and gives one extra lamport to the first `remainder` sides, storing the exact per-side total and mirroring it into the creator's bets, so side totals agree with total_pool at creation with no change to seeds, account layout, instruction set or fee split. Blast radius is one instruction in one file; the cost is a deterministic one-lamport skew toward the earliest side indices. Nothing here is accepted, and no behavioural validation is claimed - the supplied fixture is build-only.
risks: Build-only fixture is the central limitation: compilation and attestation are the only things the supplied evidence covers. No supplied evidence exercises create_market, side totals, creator bets or a payout at runtime, so the lamport-stranding mechanism is a code reading and not an observation.

The candidate changes creation-time accounting only. Markets already created with a residue are not repaired - nothing here recovers lamports that an existing market fails to attribute, and no migration or close path is built or proposed as part of this package.

Ordering dependence is a real risk of the chosen alternative: which sides receive the extra lamport follows the order of side_names as supplied. Any client that recomputes a quotient for display, or asserts a 'first side' total, will surface a one-lamport difference. Whether the hosted devnet app recomputes side splits client-side was not read in this task.
claim_winnings multiplies in u128 before dividing, so the candidate adds no new rounding but its overflow boundary at extreme pool sizes was not analysed and is not claimed safe here.

The defect remains in upstream main as read today, so nothing in this package should be read as an upstream fix in force; upstream movement depends on an ordinary pull request the upstream author has not agreed to.

Scope of this response: narrative sections only. I have not marked validation as passed, have not marked the contribution as accepted, and hold no credential claim to make - the recorded workflow conclusion belongs to the build-and-attest jobs of a build-only fixture.
narrative.rollback: Rollback is a single revert of b3248454 on lab main. There is no migration: the instruction set, account layouts, seeds and fee arithmetic are unchanged, and the candidate reads and writes only fields that already existed. State implications, stated plainly: markets created under the candidate store side totals that already sum to total_pool, so they keep reconciling and their claims compute normally after a revert; markets created after a revert return to truncated accounting, where a residue is again unreachable. The honest cost of rolling back is not state damage but the loss of the reconciliation property for every market created afterwards. Verification on revert: create a market under the candidate on a local validator, record its side totals, revert, then bet, resolve and claim against that pre-existing market and confirm payouts use the stored totals and the market drains to zero.
